"He who formerly walked with a staff in hand is now a deer-hunter;
through hope, he has fallen into a terrible mire."
She was unable to reach the other shore.
Thinking me to be completely intoxicated,
Cāpā delighted her son.
“Having severed the bond for Cāpā,
I shall go forth once again.
“Do not be angry with me, O Great Hero!”
Do not be angry with me, O Great Sage;
for one who is overcome by anger,
there is no purity— how then can there be asceticism?
“Even as one departs from the reed-thicket,
anger follows along with the reed;
they bind one by means of the form of a woman.”
“Come back, Kāḷa! Return and enjoy sensual pleasures as before, you ascetic who lives by the Dhamma.”
“I have brought you under my control,
as well as those who are my kinsmen.
“From this, O lute, take one-fourth;”
Just as you have spoken to me:
for a person who delights in you,
that would indeed be sublime.”
Like a kāḷaṅginī plant or a takkārī tree in full bloom atop a mountain,
like a blossoming dālima or laṭṭhī tree—
Like a *pāṭalī* tree in the middle of an island—
her limbs anointed with yellow sandalwood and wearing the finest Kāsī cloth.
“Leaving me here, beautiful and at peace,
where are you going? “I am like a fowler leaving a bird,” she replied.
Just as one might wish to bind me with a form that is not pleasing,
you shall not afflict me.
“O Kāḷa, this fruit of a son has been produced for me by you;
thus, let me remain as one who possesses a son.”
“Whom do you leave behind as you go?
“The wise abandon their children,
and from them their relatives, and from them their wealth.”
“The great heroes go forth,
like an elephant that has severed its bonds.
“Now, my son, this child of yours— ”
"With a staff or with a knife,
or by crushing you upon the ground,
you shall not escape from the grief for your son."
“If you go to the dogs and jackals as a son, then,
O wretched woman, you will not be my son.”
“Will you return again?
“Well then, venerable sir,
where will Kāḷa go now?”
“What village, town,
city, or royal capital was it?
“In the past, we were leaders of a group.”
Not being ascetics, yet imagining ourselves to be ascetics,
we wandered from village to village and through royal capitals in the cities.
For this Blessed One, the Buddha,
has come to the river Nerañjarā for the sake of abandoning all suffering.
He teaches the Dhamma to living beings;
I shall go into his presence,
for he will be my teacher.”
"Now you should offer salutation to the unsurpassed Lord of the World,
and having performed a circumambulation,"
"You should designate the sacrificial gift.
"This indeed is obtainable for us,
just as you have spoken to me;"
Now, having paid homage to you,
the unsurpassed Lord of the World,
and having performed a circumambulation, [I shall depart].
"I shall explain the gift.
Then Kāḷa departed toward the river Nerañjarā.
Thus he saw the Fully Awakened One teaching the state of deathlessness:
suffering and the origin of suffering.
And the transcendence of suffering;
the Noble Eightfold Path that leads to the stilling of suffering.
Having paid homage at his feet and circumambulated him to the right,
he pointed out Cāpā.
I went forth into the homeless life;
the three knowledges have been attained,
and the teaching of the Buddha has been accomplished.
… The Elder Nun Cāpā …
